definitions.explanation: The state of fruit (or sometimes other produce) being completely ripened on the plant or after picking. Often used as a marketing term to advertise produce at peak flavor.

examples.japanese: {完熟|かんじゅく}のトマトは{甘|あま}い。
このマンゴーは{完熟|かんじゅく}してから{食|た}べると{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: These mangoes are delicious if you eat them after they've fully ripened.

examples.japanese: {農家|のうか}は{完熟|かんじゅく}{果実|かじつ}だけを{選|えら}んで{出荷|しゅっか}している。
examples.english: The farmers select and ship only fully ripened fruit.

notes:
Compound of {完|かん} (complete) + {熟|じゅく} (ripen, mature). Used both as a noun and as a する verb ({完熟|かんじゅく}する, 'to become fully ripe'); the prenominal form {完熟|かんじゅく}の or {完熟|かんじゅく}した modifies the produce.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {完熟|かんじゅく}トマト: fully ripe tomato
- {完熟|かんじゅく}マンゴー: fully ripe mango
- {完熟|かんじゅく}{果実|かじつ}: ripe fruit (marketing phrase)
- {完熟|かんじゅく}する: to ripen fully

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {熟|じゅく}す: to ripen (general verb)
- {熟|う}れる: to ripen (intransitive, more colloquial)
- {未熟|みじゅく}: unripe; immature (antonym)
